why: Same task as TikTok's 'Build Blocks from a Starting Position': a block [x, x + size - 1] fits iff the first obstacle at or after x is beyond x + size - 1. Keep obstacles sorted and binary search; the 'design' part of the week is choosing that sorted structure.
hints: For a check at x you only care about one obstacle. Which one?
The smallest obstacle >= x. The block fits iff that obstacle does not exist or is > x + size - 1.
Sorted list + bisect_left per query (or a SortedList / TreeSet for O(log n) inserts). Append '1' or '0' per type-2 operation.
pitfalls: Block cells are x .. x + size - 1, inclusive.
An obstacle at exactly x makes the answer 0.
Do not mark each cell of the block; sizes can be large.
statement:
On an infinite number line you process a list of operations:

  • [1, x]: place an obstacle at coordinate x (x is guaranteed to be empty).
  • [2, x, size]: check whether a block of length size starting at x could be built, i.e. whether all of x, x+1, ..., x+size-1 are free of obstacles. Output '1' if they are, '0' otherwise. The block is not actually built.

Return the string formed by the outputs of all type-2 operations, in order.

Example: [[1,2],[1,5],[2,3,2],[2,3,3],[2,1,1],[2,1,2]]

  • Obstacles at 2 and 5.
  • [2,3,2]: cells 3, 4 are free: 1.
  • [2,3,3]: cells 3, 4, 5; 5 has an obstacle: 0.
  • [2,1,1]: cell 1 is free: 1.
  • [2,1,2]: cells 1, 2; 2 has an obstacle: 0.

The answer is "1010".
constraints:
• 1 <= operations.length <= 10^5 (not stated in the source)
  • -10^9 <= x <= 10^9, 1 <= size <= 10^9 (not stated in the source)
